words.enDefinition: a person who freely offers to do something or take part in a service

examples.en: My neighbour works as a volunteer at the animal shelter every Saturday.
examples.zh: 我的邻居每周六都在动物收容所做「志愿者」。

examples.en: We need a volunteer to collect the tickets before the show starts.
examples.zh: 演出开始前，我们需要一位「志愿者」去收票。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to a national legislature (congress)

examples.en: The congressional hearing was broadcast live, so we watched it after dinner.
examples.zh: 这场「国会的」听证会全程直播，我们晚饭后看了。

examples.en: Her father spent twenty years on a congressional committee before retiring.
examples.zh: 她父亲退休前在一家「国会」委员会工作了二十年。

words.enDefinition: the state of being allied or confederated

examples.en: The two small bookshops formed an alliance to compete with the big online stores.
examples.zh: 这两家小书店结成「联盟」，与大型网店竞争。

examples.en: Our neighbourhood association broke its alliance with the recycling company over missed pickups.
examples.zh: 因为几次没能按时收运，社区协会终止了与回收公司的「联盟」关系。

words.enDefinition: someone in an official position of authority who can command or control others

examples.en: The base commander shook hands with each recruit at the graduation ceremony.
examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，「司令官」与新兵们一一握手。

examples.en: As fire commander, she decides which crew takes the truck out first.
examples.zh: 作为消防「指挥官」，由她决定哪个班组先出动消防车。

words.enDefinition: mental or emotional as opposed to physical in nature

examples.en: Losing her job took a real psychological toll on her confidence.
examples.zh: 失业给她的自信心带来了不小的「心理」创伤。

examples.en: The coach hired a psychologist to handle the team's psychological pressure.
examples.zh: 教练请了一位心理学家来疏导全队的「心理」压力。

words.enDefinition: rocket carrying a warhead of conventional or nuclear explosives; may be ballistic or directed by remote control

examples.en: The museum displays a missile that was decommissioned back in the eighties.
examples.zh: 博物馆里陈列着一枚八十年代退役的「导弹」。

examples.en: Radar tracked the missile for a few minutes before losing contact.
examples.zh: 雷达追踪那枚「导弹」几分钟后就失去了信号。

words.enDefinition: serviceman who has seen considerable active service

examples.en: Grandpa, a veteran of the Pacific war, still marches in the remembrance parade.
examples.zh: 爷爷是参加过太平洋战争的「老兵」，至今仍会参加纪念游行。

examples.en: The war veteran visits our school every autumn to share his stories.
examples.zh: 那位「老兵」每年秋天都会来学校讲他当年的故事。

words.enDefinition: person who is of equal standing with another in a group

examples.en: Teenagers often feel pressure to dress like their peers at school.
examples.zh: 青少年常常迫于压力，想穿得和「同龄人」一样。

examples.en: In group therapy, everyone sits as a peer rather than as doctor and patient.
examples.zh: 在团体治疗中，每个人都以「同辈」的身份参与，而不是医患关系。

words.enDefinition: a person who plans the look or structure of something before it is made

examples.en: The dress designer sketched three gowns before choosing one for the bride.
examples.zh: 服装「设计师」画了三张礼服草图，最后为新娘选定了其中一张。

examples.en: My cousin is a game designer who tests every level herself.
examples.zh: 我表姐是游戏「设计师」，每个关卡她都会亲自试玩。

words.zhGloss: 十三岁到十九岁的少年
words.enDefinition: juvenile between the onset of puberty and maturity
acceptedZhAnswers: 十三岁到十九岁的少年

examples.en: Our teenager spends half the evening chatting with friends on his phone.
examples.zh: 我家那个「十几岁的孩子」每晚有一半时间都在手机上和朋友聊天。

examples.en: The library runs a quiet study room just for teenagers after school.
examples.zh: 图书馆放学后专门为「青少年」开放一间安静的自习室。

words.enDefinition: an expert who observes and comments on something

examples.en: As a quiet observer, she notices details everyone else misses at family gatherings.
examples.zh: 作为一个安静的「观察者」，她能注意到家庭聚会上别人忽略的细节。

examples.en: Election officials invited international observers to watch the polling stations.
examples.zh: 选举官员邀请了国际「观察员」监督各投票站。

words.enDefinition: belonging to the past; of what is important or famous in the past

examples.en: They restored the historic theatre instead of tearing it down for a car park.
examples.zh: 他们修复了那座「有历史意义的」剧院，而不是拆掉改建停车场。

examples.en: Walking across the historic bridge feels like stepping back a century.
examples.zh: 走过这座「历史悠久的」桥，仿佛回到了一百年前。

words.enDefinition: leaping insect; male makes chirping noises by rubbing the forewings together

examples.en: A cricket kept me awake all night with its chirping outside the window.
examples.zh: 一只「蟋蟀」在窗外叫了一整夜，吵得我没睡着。

examples.en: The kids caught a cricket in the garden and kept it in a box.
examples.zh: 孩子们在花园里捉到一只「蟋蟀」，把它养在了盒子里。

words.enDefinition: of or relating to or characteristic of literature

examples.en: Her literary tastes run to old detective novels rather than modern fiction.
examples.zh: 她的「文学」品味偏向老派侦探小说，而不是当代作品。

examples.en: The city's literary festival draws poets and readers from all over the country.
examples.zh: 这座城市的「文学」节吸引着全国的诗人和读者。

words.enDefinition: stringed instrument usually having six strings; played by strumming or plucking

examples.en: He bought an old guitar at the flea market and taught himself chords.
examples.zh: 他在跳蚤市场买了一把旧「吉他」，自学和弦。

examples.en: She sings at the cafe every Friday, with her guitar on her knee.
examples.zh: 每周五她都会把「吉他」放在膝上，在咖啡馆里唱歌。

words.enDefinition: correctional institution used to detain persons who are in the lawful custody of the government (either accused persons awaiting trial or convicted persons serving a sentence)

examples.en: He spent a night in jail for refusing to pay the fine.
examples.zh: 他因拒缴罚款在「拘留所」里待了一晚。

examples.en: The old jail is now a museum with guided tours.
examples.zh: 那座旧「监狱」如今成了提供导览的博物馆。

words.enDefinition: reason for wanting something done

examples.en: For the sake of her health, Dad finally gave up smoking.
examples.zh: 出于她健康的「缘故」，爸爸终于把烟戒了。

examples.en: They kept the old piano for the sake of their mother's memories.
examples.zh: 为了母亲那份回忆的「缘故」，他们留下了那架旧钢琴。

words.enDefinition: an electrical device that provides a path for electrical current to flow

examples.en: The fuse blew because the circuit was overloaded with two heaters.
examples.zh: 「电路」上同时接了两台取暖器，超负荷把保险丝烧断了。

examples.en: Dad traced the broken circuit in the garage light with a screwdriver and tape.
examples.zh: 爸爸用螺丝刀和胶带，查出了车库灯「电路」的故障点。

words.enDefinition: to voluntarily leave a job or position

examples.en: She decided to resign after the company refused her flexible-hours request twice.
examples.zh: 公司两次拒绝她的弹性工时请求后，她决定「辞职」。

examples.en: The head coach announced he would resign at the end of the season.
examples.zh: 主教练宣布赛季结束后将「辞职」。

words.enDefinition: a large area of a country with its own local government

examples.en: Sichuan is the province my grandmother still calls home after all these years.
examples.zh: 这么多年过去，四川仍是奶奶口中那个「省」、那个家。

examples.en: The new high-speed rail will link that province to the capital in three hours.
examples.zh: 新的高铁将使那个「省」在三小时内直达首都。

words.enDefinition: political advocate of socialism

examples.en: My uncle is a socialist who believes hospitals should be free for everyone.
examples.zh: 我叔叔是个「社会主义者」，他认为医疗应当对全民免费。

examples.en: The young socialist handed out leaflets about rent control outside the station.
examples.zh: 那位年轻的「社会主义者」在车站外分发租金管制的传单。

words.enDefinition: to break suddenly with a sharp cracking sound

examples.en: The old clothesline snapped under the weight of the wet blankets.
examples.zh: 晒衣绳被湿毯子一压，就「啪地断了」。

examples.en: She snapped the chocolate bar in half and handed me the bigger piece.
examples.zh: 她把巧克力「啪地掰成」两半，把大的那半递给了我。

words.enDefinition: someone who causes the death of a person or animal

examples.en: Police finally caught the killer after three years of investigating.
examples.zh: 经过三年侦查，警方终于抓获了那名「杀人者」。

examples.en: Detectives questioned neighbours hoping someone had seen the killer leave the building.
examples.zh: 侦探们询问邻居，希望有人见过「凶手」离开大楼。

words.enDefinition: writer of poems (the term is usually reserved for writers of good poetry)

examples.en: Grandmother was a poet who wrote about the harbour and her childhood.
examples.zh: 奶奶是一位「诗人」，写海港，也写童年。

examples.en: The cafe hosts an open night where any poet can read their work.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆办开放夜，任何「诗人」都可以上台朗读作品。

words.enDefinition: an association of criminals

examples.en: The police broke up a gang that had been stealing bicycles in the district.
examples.zh: 警方捣毁了一个长期在本区偷自行车的「犯罪团伙」。

examples.en: He grew up on a street where joining a gang seemed the only option.
examples.zh: 他长大的那条街上，加入「帮派」似乎是唯一的选择。

words.enDefinition: widely circulated or diffused

examples.en: Power cuts are widespread in the region after the storm.
examples.zh: 风暴过后，这个地区「普遍」停电。

examples.en: There is widespread support among parents for the later school start time.
examples.zh: 家长们「普遍」支持学校把上课时间推迟。

words.enDefinition: person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea

examples.en: She is a passionate advocate for cheaper public transport in our city.
examples.zh: 她是我们市里主张降低公交票价的坚定「提倡者」。

examples.en: As a tenants' advocate, he helps people fight unfair rent increases.
examples.zh: 作为房客权益「倡导者」，他帮助人们对抗不合理的涨租。

words.enDefinition: to a moderately sufficient extent or degree

examples.en: The plumber explained the costs reasonably, so we trusted his quote.
examples.zh: 水管工把费用解释得「合情合理」，我们便信了他的报价。

examples.en: You can find a used bike reasonably cheap if you shop in spring.
examples.zh: 如果春天去淘，二手自行车能买到「相当」便宜的。

words.enDefinition: an actor with a small background part in a film or play

examples.en: Her first job in the city was as a super in a crowded street scene.
examples.zh: 她进城后的第一份工作，是在一个拥挤的街景镜头里当「跑龙套的群众演员」。

examples.en: The director shouted at the supers to keep moving behind the main actors.
examples.zh: 导演朝「群众演员」们喊话，要他们在主演身后继续走动。

words.enDefinition: any likeness of a person, in any medium

examples.en: The artist charged a modest fee to paint a portrait of the couple.
examples.zh: 画家收了笔不高的费用，为这对夫妇画了一幅「肖像」。

examples.en: A portrait of the town's founder hangs in the library entrance.
examples.zh: 图书馆入口处挂着一幅小镇创始人的「肖像画」。

words.enDefinition: an onerous or difficult concern

examples.en: Carrying the groceries alone became a burden on her sore shoulder.
examples.zh: 独自搬这堆采购的东西，成了她酸痛肩膀上的一份「负担」。

examples.en: He didn't want his debts to become a burden for his children.
examples.zh: 他不想让自己的债务变成孩子们的「负担」。

words.enDefinition: a short description of a person's life, character, or activities

examples.en: She updated her work profile before applying for the design job.
examples.zh: 申请那份设计工作前，她先更新了自己的职业「简介」。

examples.en: The magazine published a profile of the baker who rebuilt his shop after the fire.
examples.zh: 杂志刊登了一篇「人物特写」，讲的是火灾后重建店铺的面包师。

words.enDefinition: a person who operates a machine, switchboard, or piece of equipment

examples.en: The crane operator signalled to the ground crew before lifting the steel beam.
examples.zh: 吊车「操作员」在起吊钢梁前，先向地面人员打手势。

examples.en: Dial zero and the operator will connect you to the pharmacy.
examples.zh: 拨零，接线「员」会帮你转接到药房。

words.enDefinition: make strong or stronger

examples.en: These weekly walks will strengthen your legs before the mountain trip.
examples.zh: 出发爬山前，每周的这些步行能「增强」你的腿部力量。

examples.en: The bank strengthened its security after several customers reported suspicious calls.
examples.zh: 多位客户接到可疑电话后，银行「加强」了安全防范。

words.enDefinition: an act of cleaning or drying something by rubbing it with a cloth

examples.en: Give the table a quick wipe before the guests arrive.
examples.zh: 客人到来之前，把桌子快速「擦」一遍。

examples.en: One wipe with a damp cloth removed the fingerprints from the screen.
examples.zh: 用湿布「擦」一下，屏幕上的指纹就没了。

words.enDefinition: businessperson engaged in retail trade

examples.en: The old merchant on the corner sells spices he grinds himself.
examples.zh: 街角那位年长的「商人」卖的是自己研磨的香料。

examples.en: Silk merchants once travelled this dangerous mountain pass every spring.
examples.zh: 从前每年春天，丝绸「商人」都会翻越这段险峻的山口。

words.enDefinition: sporting competition in which contestants play a series of games to decide the winner

examples.en: Our chess club will host a tournament in the community hall next month.
examples.zh: 我们的象棋俱乐部下月将在社区礼堂举办一场「锦标赛」。

examples.en: She twisted her ankle in the first round of the tennis tournament.
examples.zh: 网球「赛」第一轮她就扭伤了脚踝。

words.enDefinition: extremely large, great, or impressive in amount or intensity

examples.en: There was a tremendous turnout for the neighbourhood cleanup on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六的社区清扫活动来了「多得惊人的」人手。

examples.en: The new bakery faces tremendous competition from the chain next door.
examples.zh: 这家新面包店面临隔壁连锁店的「巨大」竞争压力。

words.enDefinition: supply with necessities and support

examples.en: A bowl of oatmeal sustains me through the whole morning shift.
examples.zh: 一碗燕麦粥能「支撑」我熬过整个早班。

examples.en: The monthly donations sustain the small shelter and its thirty residents.
examples.zh: 每月的捐款「维持」着这家小收容所和里面三十位住客的生计。

words.enDefinition: any of various platforms built into a vessel

examples.en: Passengers lined the deck to watch the island appear through the morning fog.
examples.zh: 乘客们聚集在「甲板」上，看着岛屿在晨雾中显现。

examples.en: The crew scrubbed the deck every morning before the tourists came aboard.
examples.zh: 游客登船前，船员每天早上都会擦洗「甲板」。

words.enDefinition: conversation between two persons

examples.en: The manager sat down with the staff for an honest dialogue about the schedule.
examples.zh: 经理和员工坐下来，就排班问题进行了一次坦诚的「对话」。

examples.en: Good dialogue in a novel makes the characters feel alive.
examples.zh: 小说里写得好的「对话」，会让角色显得活灵活现。

words.enDefinition: form of football played with an oval ball

examples.en: He played rugby every winter until his knees finally gave out.
examples.zh: 他每年冬天都打「橄榄球」，直到膝盖撑不住为止。

examples.en: The rugby team trains on the muddy field behind the school.
examples.zh: 「橄榄球队」在学校后面那片泥泞的场地上训练。

words.enDefinition: smallest army unit

examples.en: Our five-a-side squad meets in the park every Tuesday evening.
examples.zh: 我们这支五人「小队」每周二晚上都在公园里聚练。

examples.en: The captain chose the squad a week before the regional finals.
examples.zh: 区域决赛前一周，队长就定下了参赛「小队」名单。

words.enDefinition: with a possibility of becoming actual

examples.en: Leaving the stove on overnight could potentially start a fire.
examples.zh: 炉子彻夜开着，「有可能」引发火灾。

examples.en: The flooded road is potentially impassable, so take the longer route.
examples.zh: 被淹的那条路「可能」无法通行，还是绕远路吧。

words.enDefinition: with regard to social relationships involving authority

examples.en: The union vote was politically sensitive, so the manager stayed neutral.
examples.zh: 工会投票在「政治上」很敏感，经理保持了中立。

examples.en: Grandparents often discuss politically charged news topics at Sunday dinner.
examples.zh: 周日晚餐时，祖父母常常谈论「政治上」有争议的新闻话题。

words.enDefinition: an unshakable belief in something without need for proof or evidence

examples.en: Her conviction that kindness changes people kept her volunteering at the shelter.
examples.zh: 她「深信」善良能改变人，这份信念让她一直坚持在收容所做义工。

examples.en: He spoke about the scheme with real conviction, and the committee approved it.
examples.zh: 他「满怀信念」地谈起这个方案，委员会随即批准了。

words.enDefinition: radical who employs terror as a political weapon; usually organizes with other terrorists in small cells; often uses religion as a cover for terrorist activities

examples.en: The news showed the damage after the terrorist attack on the station.
examples.zh: 新闻播出了车站遭「恐怖分子」袭击后的损毁画面。

examples.en: Security was tightened at the airport following warnings about terrorist activity.
examples.zh: 由于收到有关「恐怖分子」活动的警告，机场加强了安检。

words.enDefinition: game played with rackets by two or four players who hit a ball back and forth over a net that divides the court

examples.en: We booked the tennis court for Saturday morning, as usual.
examples.zh: 我们照常订了周六上午的「网球」场地。

examples.en: She plays tennis twice a week to stay fit after work.
examples.zh: 下班后她每周打两次「网球」来保持身材。

words.enDefinition: person who uses the mind creatively

examples.en: The salon drew every intellectual in town to debate the new library plan.
examples.zh: 沙龙把镇上所有「知识分子」都吸引来讨论新图书馆方案。

examples.en: As a public intellectual, he explains philosophy on the radio every Sunday.
examples.zh: 作为公众「知识分子」，他每周日在电台讲解哲学。

words.enDefinition: close fighting during the culmination of a military attack

examples.en: The fortress withstood a fierce assault for three days before reinforcements arrived.
examples.zh: 堡垒顶住了三天猛烈的「进攻」，援军才赶到。

examples.en: Soldiers rehearsed the dawn assault on the ridge using a sand table.
examples.zh: 士兵们用沙盘推演拂晓对山脊发起「强攻」的行动。

words.enDefinition: contentious speech act; a dispute where there is strong disagreement

examples.en: The decision to close the pool sparked fresh controversy in town.
examples.zh: 关闭游泳池的决定在镇上再度引发「争议」。

examples.en: The documentary caused controversy abroad but was praised at home.
examples.zh: 这部纪录片在国外引发「争议」，在国内却广受好评。

words.enDefinition: gradually ceasing to be visible

examples.en: The photo on the windowsill has faded to pale grey after ten summers.
examples.zh: 窗台上的照片晒了十个夏天，「褪色」成了浅灰色。

examples.en: Let the dye set overnight so the colour doesn't fade in the wash.
examples.zh: 让染料静置一夜，这样洗的时候颜色就不会「褪掉」。

words.enDefinition: drama in which the protagonist is overcome by some superior force or circumstance; excites terror or pity

examples.en: The fire that destroyed the old mill was a tragedy for the village.
examples.zh: 烧毁老磨坊的那场大火，对整个村子来说是一场「悲剧」。

examples.en: In Shakespeare's tragedy, the feud ends only when both families lose their children.
examples.zh: 在这部莎士比亚「悲剧」中，两家的世仇直到双双失去孩子才了结。

words.enDefinition: motion of hands or body to emphasize or help to express a thought or feeling

examples.en: He gave a thumbs-up gesture to show the builder he approved the design.
examples.zh: 他朝施工者比了个竖大拇指的「手势」，表示认可这个设计。

examples.en: In Italy, a simple hand gesture can say more than a sentence.
examples.zh: 在意大利，一个简单的手部「手势」有时比一句话表达得还多。

words.enDefinition: covering to disguise or conceal the face

examples.en: The children made a paper mask for the school costume party.
examples.zh: 孩子们为学校的化装派对做了一副纸「面具」。

examples.en: He wore a horror mask to scare his sister on Halloween night.
examples.zh: 万圣节晚上，他戴着恐怖「面具」去吓妹妹。

words.enDefinition: having a quality that thrusts itself into attention

examples.en: The mayor hung the artist's painting in the most prominent spot in the hall.
examples.zh: 市长把这位画家的作品挂在大厅最「显眼」的位置。

examples.en: She is a prominent lawyer who often argues cases on live television.
examples.zh: 她是「声名显赫的」律师，常在电视直播中出庭辩论。

words.enDefinition: police officer who investigates crimes

examples.en: The detective studied the muddy footprints leading away from the garden gate.
examples.zh: 「侦探」仔细查看花园门外一路远去的泥泞脚印。

examples.en: My niece reads nothing but detective stories before going to sleep.
examples.zh: 我侄女睡前只看「侦探」小说。

words.enDefinition: an event (or a course of events) that will inevitably happen in the future

examples.en: Meeting her future husband on a delayed train felt like fate.
examples.zh: 在晚点的火车上遇到未来的丈夫，仿佛是「命运」的安排。

examples.en: The old fisherman believes the sea decides a sailor's fate.
examples.zh: 老渔民相信，水手的「命运」由大海决定。

words.enDefinition: one of the parts into which something naturally divides

examples.en: The final segment of the documentary shows the villagers rebuilding the bridge.
examples.zh: 纪录片的最后一段「片段」，呈现了村民重建桥梁的过程。

examples.en: The radio show plays a jazz segment between the news and the weather.
examples.zh: 电台节目在新闻和天气预报之间安排了一段爵士乐「板块」。

words.enDefinition: occurring from time to time

examples.en: An occasional glass of wine with dinner suits us fine.
examples.zh: 晚餐时「偶尔」喝一杯葡萄酒，我们就挺满足了。

examples.en: He pays his occasional visits to the chess club on rainy afternoons.
examples.zh: 雨天的下午，他会「偶尔」去象棋俱乐部看看。

words.enDefinition: run away quickly

examples.en: The villagers fled to higher ground when the river banks broke.
examples.zh: 河堤决口时，村民们「逃往」高处。

examples.en: Thousands fled the burning city with whatever they could carry.
examples.zh: 成千上万的人「逃离」燃烧的城市，只带着随身能拿的东西。

words.enDefinition: take hold of; grab

examples.en: The police may seize a driver's licence after repeated drink-driving offences.
examples.zh: 多次酒驾之后，警方可能会「查扣」违规者的驾照。

examples.en: Seize the chance to ask the baker about her sourdough starter.
examples.zh: 「抓住」机会，问问面包师傅她那块天然酵母的来历。

words.enDefinition: drama set to music; consists of singing with orchestral accompaniment and an orchestral overture and interludes

examples.en: Grandmother introduced me to opera with a recording of The Magic Flute.
examples.zh: 奶奶用《魔笛》的唱片带我走进了「歌剧」的世界。

examples.en: The opera house offers cheap standing tickets for students on weekdays.
examples.zh: 「歌剧院」平日为学生提供便宜的站票。

words.enDefinition: in a place across an ocean

examples.en: Her son moved overseas for work and calls home every Sunday.
examples.zh: 儿子「远在海外」工作，每周日都会往家里打电话。

examples.en: The firm opened an overseas office in Singapore to reach new customers.
examples.zh: 公司在新加坡开设了「海外」办事处，以开拓新客户。

words.enDefinition: in addition to; apart from (also used as an adverb meaning “moreover”)

examples.en: Besides English, she speaks enough Spanish to order dinner abroad.
examples.zh: 「除了」英语，她的西班牙语也够在国外点餐了。

examples.en: Besides the rent, we share the cost of internet and electricity.
examples.zh: 「除了」房租，网费和电费我们也一起分摊。

words.enDefinition: beyond belief or understanding

examples.en: The street performer juggled five flaming torches, and it looked incredible.
examples.zh: 街头艺人同时抛耍五支燃烧的火把，看着真是「难以置信」。

examples.en: Grandma recovered at an incredible speed after her hip operation.
examples.zh: 髋部手术后，奶奶以「惊人的」速度康复了。

words.enDefinition: high-speed military or naval airplane designed to destroy enemy aircraft in the air

examples.en: The vintage fighter was restored by volunteers and flew again last spring.
examples.zh: 那架老式「战斗机」由志愿者修复，去年春天重新上了天。

examples.en: Two fighter jets escorted the passenger plane into the regional airport.
examples.zh: 两架「战斗机」护送客机降落在地区机场。

words.enDefinition: someone who hunts game

examples.en: The hunter waited three hours in the cold for a clear shot.
examples.zh: 「猎人」在寒风中等了三个小时，只为一枪命中的机会。

examples.en: Treasure hunters combed the beach with metal detectors after the storm.
examples.zh: 风暴过后，寻宝「猎人」们拿着金属探测器在沙滩上搜寻。

words.enDefinition: a bold or remarkable act or achievement

examples.en: The explorer's journals describe his exploits crossing the desert twice.
examples.zh: 探险家的日记记述了他两次横穿沙漠的「功绩」。

examples.en: Grandfather loves recounting his exploits as a young sailor in the north seas.
examples.zh: 爷爷最爱讲他年轻时在北方海域的「英勇事迹」。

words.enDefinition: property that is leased or rented out or let

examples.en: Our lease runs until March, so we have time to find a new flat.
examples.zh: 我们的「租约」到三月份才到期，还有时间另找房子。

examples.en: Read the lease carefully before signing anything about pets or subletting.
examples.zh: 签任何有关宠物或转租的条款前，先仔细读一遍「租约」。

words.enDefinition: disgraceful gossip about the private lives of other people

examples.en: The accounting scandal forced the charity's directors to step down.
examples.zh: 这起账目「丑闻」迫使慈善机构的理事们卸任。

examples.en: Villagers still gossip about the wedding scandal from thirty years ago.
examples.zh: 村民们至今还在议论三十年前那桩婚礼「丑闻」。

words.enDefinition: document incorporating an institution and specifying its rights; includes the articles of incorporation and the certificate of incorporation

examples.en: The club rewrote its charter to allow junior members under sixteen.
examples.zh: 俱乐部修改了「章程」，允许十六岁以下的少年加入。

examples.en: The city granted a charter to the fishermen's cooperative in 1902.
examples.zh: 1902 年，市政当局向渔业合作社颁发了「特许状」。

words.enDefinition: traditional story accepted as history; serves to explain the world view of a people

examples.en: Grandmother told us the myth of the sea serpent who guards the harbour.
examples.zh: 奶奶给我们讲过看守海港的大海蛇「神话」。

examples.en: In Greek myth, Prometheus stole fire from the gods for humankind.
examples.zh: 在希腊「神话」中，普罗米修斯为人类盗取了火种。

words.enDefinition: tube through which a bullet travels when a gun is fired

examples.en: He cleaned the rifle's barrel with an oiled rod after every hunt.
examples.zh: 每次打猎后，他都会用蘸油的通条清理枪「管」。

examples.en: The collector confirmed the barrel was original and the stock was newer.
examples.zh: 收藏家确认枪「管」是原装的，枪托则是后来配的。

words.enDefinition: an utterance made by exhaling audibly

examples.en: She let out a deep sigh and finally closed the textbook.
examples.zh: 她长长地「叹」了一口气，终于合上了课本。

examples.en: A relieved sigh escaped him when the dentist said no fillings were needed.
examples.zh: 听到牙医说不用补牙，他如释重负地「舒了一口气」。

words.enDefinition: marked by or capable of arousing controversy

examples.en: The plan to cut the old oak tree proved controversial at the meeting.
examples.zh: 砍伐老橡树的计划在会上「很有争议」。

examples.en: Her controversial remarks about the referee spread quickly among fans.
examples.zh: 她关于裁判的「争议言论」很快在球迷间传开。

words.enDefinition: an aircraft without wings that obtains its lift from the rotation of overhead blades

examples.en: A rescue helicopter lifted the stranded hikers off the mountain at dusk.
examples.zh: 黄昏时分，救援「直升机」把被困的登山者吊离了山区。

examples.en: The children ran to the fence every time a helicopter passed overhead.
examples.zh: 每当有「直升机」飞过，孩子们都会跑到栅栏边去看。

words.enDefinition: having or showing keen interest or intense desire or impatient expectancy

examples.en: The puppies were eager to explore every corner of the garden.
examples.zh: 小狗们「急切地」想探索花园的每个角落。

examples.en: She was eager to start her new job at the village clinic.
examples.zh: 她迫切盼着去村里的诊所开始新工作。

words.enDefinition: government administrator

examples.en: The police commissioner promised more foot patrols in the old quarter.
examples.zh: 警察「总监」承诺在老城区增加步行巡逻。

examples.en: The planning commissioner approved the housing project after two hearings.
examples.zh: 规划「专员」在两次听证会后批准了住宅项目。

words.enDefinition: form the substance of

examples.en: Retired teachers and nurses compose most of the village's volunteer brigade.
examples.zh: 村里的志愿队主要由退休教师和护士「组成」。

examples.en: Twelve neighbourhood volunteers compose the cleanup crew every spring.
examples.zh: 每年春天，十二名社区志愿者「组成」清扫队。

words.enDefinition: in another and different manner;

examples.en: The twins approach the same puzzle differently, and both methods work.
examples.zh: 这对双胞胎解同一道谜题的「方式各不相同」，但两种方法都行得通。

examples.en: People read the same message differently depending on their mood.
examples.zh: 心情不同，人们对同一条信息的理解也会「不一样」。

words.enDefinition: motor vehicle with four wheels; usually propelled by an internal combustion engine

examples.en: His first car was a battered auto he bought from a neighbour.
examples.zh: 他的第一辆「汽车」是从邻居手里买下的一辆破旧车。

examples.en: The old auto factory now houses a weekend flea market.
examples.zh: 那座旧「汽车」厂房如今成了周末跳蚤市场的场地。

words.enDefinition: a person who engages in or supports a revolution

examples.en: The young revolutionary printed pamphlets in the cellar of the bakery.
examples.zh: 那位年轻的「革命者」在面包房的地窖里印刷传单。

examples.en: Museum exhibits trace how the revolutionaries organised the coastal towns.
examples.zh: 博物馆展品追溯了「革命者」们如何组织沿海城镇。

words.enDefinition: a time of rapid growth, increase, or success

examples.en: The fishing town enjoyed a tourist boom after the ferry line opened.
examples.zh: 轮渡航线开通后，这座渔镇迎来了旅游「热潮」。

examples.en: The baby boom of the sixties filled every school in the valley.
examples.zh: 六十年代的生育「高峰」让山谷里每所学校都满了。

words.enDefinition: total income or amount before any deductions

examples.en: Our bakery's gross rose after we added Sunday hours.
examples.zh: 增加周日营业时间后，我们面包店的「总收入」上升了。

examples.en: The accountant compared this year's gross with last year's figure before deductions.
examples.zh: 会计把今年的「总额」与去年的税前数字做了比较。

words.enDefinition: nonmilitary citizen

examples.en: Two civilians were praised for pulling the driver from the wreck.
examples.zh: 两名「平民」因把司机从残骸中救出而受到表彰。

examples.en: After the war, the general lived quietly as a civilian in the countryside.
examples.zh: 战后，将军以「平民」身份在乡下过起了安静的日子。

words.enDefinition: to sentence someone to a punishment

examples.en: The judge condemned the smuggler to two years in prison.
examples.zh: 法官「判处」走私犯两年监禁。

examples.en: The magistrate condemned him to community service instead of jail time.
examples.zh: 治安法官「判」他用社区服务代替监禁。

words.enDefinition: statement that is emphatic and explicit (spoken or written)

examples.en: Her declaration that she would open a bookshop surprised the whole family.
examples.zh: 她宣称要开书店，这份「声明」让全家人都吃了一惊。

examples.en: The declaration of the marathon results drew cheers from the crowd.
examples.zh: 马拉松成绩的「宣布」引来了人群的欢呼。

words.enDefinition: female actor

examples.en: The actress playing the queen stayed to sign autographs for the school group.
examples.zh: 饰演女王的那位「女演员」留下来为学生们签名。

examples.en: She studied for years before landing her first role as an actress.
examples.zh: 她苦学多年，才迎来当「女演员」的第一个角色。

words.enDefinition: young person of either sex

examples.en: The camp pairs each youngster with a mentor for the summer.
examples.zh: 夏令营里，每个「孩子」都会与一位导师结伴一夏。

examples.en: Youngsters from the village crowd around the ice-cream van at noon.
examples.zh: 正午时分，村里的「孩子们」围着冰淇淋车不肯散去。

words.enDefinition: the land along the edge of a body of water

examples.en: We walked along the shore collecting shells until the sun went down.
examples.zh: 我们沿着「海岸」捡贝壳，一直走到日落。

examples.en: The cottage stands a hundred metres from the shore of the lake.
examples.zh: 小屋离湖「岸」只有一百米。

words.enDefinition: an organization formed by merging several groups or parties

examples.en: The village cricket clubs formed a federation to share pitches and equipment.
examples.zh: 各村板球俱乐部组成「联合会」，共用场地和器材。

examples.en: The federation negotiates prices for its member farms each season.
examples.zh: 「联合会」每个季度都替成员农场议价。

words.enDefinition: not extreme; limited in amount or degree

examples.en: Take a moderate pace up the hill and you won't be breathless.
examples.zh: 上山时保持「适中的」速度，就不会气喘吁吁。

examples.en: We asked for a moderate amount of chilli in the stew.
examples.zh: 我们要求炖菜里放「适度的」辣椒。

words.enDefinition: worthy of reliance or trust

examples.en: Our old van is slow but reliable on the mountain roads.
examples.zh: 我们的旧面包车虽慢，在山路上却很「可靠」。

examples.en: She's the most reliable babysitter in the neighbourhood, always on time.
examples.zh: 她是社区里最「靠谱的」保姆，从不迟到。

words.enDefinition: someone whose employment involves carrying something

examples.en: The water carrier walks the steep path to the hill village twice a day.
examples.zh: 送水「工」每天沿陡峭小路往山村送两趟水。

examples.en: Hiring extra carriers for the trek cost less than we expected.
examples.zh: 为徒步旅程雇额外的「搬运工」，花费比我们预想的少。

words.enDefinition: the periodic rise and fall of the sea level under the gravitational pull of the moon

examples.en: The tide comes in fast here, so check the timetable before swimming.
examples.zh: 这里涨「潮」很快，下水前先查好潮汐表。

examples.en: Fishermen set their crab pots according to the tide each morning.
examples.zh: 渔民每天早上按「潮汐」放置蟹笼。

words.enDefinition: unit of area (4840 square yards) used in English-speaking countries

examples.en: Their farm covers forty acres of orchard and open pasture.
examples.zh: 他们的农场有四十「英亩」果园和开阔草场。

examples.en: One acre of sunflowers turned the hillside gold in August.
examples.zh: 八月里，一「英亩」向日葵把山坡染成了金色。

words.enDefinition: written version of a play or other dramatic composition; used in preparing for a performance

examples.en: The actors highlighted their lines in the script before the first rehearsal.
examples.zh: 首次排练前，演员们先在「剧本」上标出了自己的台词。

examples.en: She carries the shooting script everywhere, full of pencil notes.
examples.zh: 她走到哪儿都带着满是铅笔批注的拍摄「剧本」。

words.enDefinition: plan for attaining a particular goal

examples.en: His favourite tactic at markets is bargaining with a smile.
examples.zh: 他在集市上最喜欢的「策略」就是笑着砍价。

examples.en: The coach's defensive tactic in the second half confused the visitors.
examples.zh: 教练下半场的防守「战术」让客队乱了阵脚。

words.enDefinition: the heading or caption of a newspaper article

examples.en: The flood made the front page headline in the regional paper.
examples.zh: 洪水成了地区报纸的头版「大标题」。

examples.en: She scans the headlines over breakfast, then reads one article properly.
examples.zh: 她早餐时浏览「新闻标题」，再挑一篇细读。

words.enDefinition: recently enlisted soldier

examples.en: The young recruit learned to fold his uniform into a tight pack.
examples.zh: 那名新「兵」学着把军装叠成紧凑的一包。

examples.en: Each recruit writes home after the first week of basic training.
examples.zh: 基础训练第一周结束后，每名「新兵」都给家里写信。

words.enDefinition: with official authorization

examples.en: The couple were formally married in the town hall on a rainy Tuesday.
examples.zh: 一个多雨的周二，这对夫妇在市政厅「正式」完婚。

examples.en: The club formally announced the new coach at Friday's meeting.
examples.zh: 俱乐部在周五的会议上「正式」公布了新教练。

words.enDefinition: make into a whole or make part of a whole

examples.en: The new library will integrate a reading room with a small cafe.
examples.zh: 新图书馆将把阅览室与一家小咖啡馆「融合」在一起。

examples.en: Immigrant families gradually integrate into the village through the school and church.
examples.zh: 移民家庭通过学校和教堂逐渐「融入」村庄。

words.enDefinition: football game in which two teams of 11 players try to kick or head a ball into the opponents' goal

examples.en: The boys organized a soccer match in the lane behind their house.
examples.zh: 男孩们在屋后的小巷里组织了一场「足球」赛。

examples.en: Saturday soccer keeps the whole neighbourhood's kids out of the house.
examples.zh: 周六的「足球」活动让整个社区的孩子们都不宅在家里。

words.enDefinition: the act of grasping or holding tightly

examples.en: The baby's grip on my finger was surprisingly strong.
examples.zh: 婴儿「紧紧抓住」我的手指，力道出奇的大。

examples.en: Adjust your grip on the racket before serving, the coach says.
examples.zh: 教练说，发球前先调整一下「握拍」。

words.enDefinition: surpassingly good

examples.en: The inn served a superb breakfast with honey from their own hives.
examples.zh: 这家客栈的早餐「棒极了」，配的是自家蜂场产的蜂蜜。

examples.en: Her superb sense of direction saved us on the foggy trail.
examples.zh: 她那「出色的」方向感在雾中小径上救了我们。

words.enDefinition: look forward to the probable occurrence of

examples.en: Fresh bread awaits customers the moment the bakery opens at seven.
examples.zh: 面包房七点一开门，新鲜的面包就在「等着」顾客了。

examples.en: The finalists now await the judges' decision in the lounge.
examples.zh: 决赛选手们此刻正在休息室「等待」评委的结果。

words.enDefinition: to weaken something gradually or secretly

examples.en: Constant criticism at home can quietly undermine a child's confidence at school.
examples.zh: 家里不断的批评会悄悄「削弱」孩子在学校里的自信。

examples.en: The leaks undermined public trust in the committee months before the election.
examples.zh: 选前数月，泄密事件「损害」了公众对委员会的信任。

words.enDefinition: an engagement fought between two military forces

examples.en: The medal honoured his bravery in hand-to-hand combat during the landing.
examples.zh: 这枚勋章表彰他在登陆作战中「肉搏」的英勇。

examples.en: Veterans of that combat still meet every year in the small hall.
examples.zh: 那场「战斗」的老兵们如今仍每年在小礼堂聚会。

words.enDefinition: the main stalk of a plant

examples.en: She cut the rose stems underwater so the flowers last longer.
examples.zh: 她在水下剪断玫瑰「花茎」，这样花能开得更久。

examples.en: Strip the lower leaves from the stem before placing it in the vase.
examples.zh: 把「茎」下部的叶子摘掉，再插进花瓶。

words.enDefinition: group of aircraft operating together under the same ownership

examples.en: The fishing fleet heads out at dawn when the harbour bell rings.
examples.zh: 港口钟声一响，捕鱼「船队」便在黎明出海。

examples.en: The bakery's delivery fleet was repainted bright green this spring.
examples.zh: 今年春天，面包房的送货「车队」全部刷成了亮绿色。

words.enDefinition: lawyer who pleads cases in court

examples.en: Her counsel advised her to settle before the case reached court.
examples.zh: 她的「律师」建议她在案子开庭前和解。

examples.en: The accused spoke only when his counsel prompted him to answer.
examples.zh: 只有当「辩护律师」提示作答时，被告才开口。

words.enDefinition: solid formed by the solidification of a chemical and having a highly regular atomic structure

examples.en: A chandelier of cut crystal catches the afternoon light in the stairwell.
examples.zh: 楼梯间里，一盏雕花「水晶」吊灯折射着午后的光线。

examples.en: The spring water runs so clear that the pebbles look like crystal.
examples.zh: 泉水清得像「水晶」一样，能看清水底的卵石。

words.enDefinition: the repetition of a sound resulting from reflection of the sound waves

examples.en: My shout came back as a faint echo from the limestone cliffs.
examples.zh: 我的呼喊从石灰岩峭壁传回微弱的「回声」。

examples.en: The canyon guides love demonstrating the echo for first-time visitors.
examples.zh: 峡谷向导最爱向初次来的游客演示「回声」。

words.enDefinition: light, self-propelled movement upwards or forwards

examples.en: With one leap, the goat cleared the gap between the rocks.
examples.zh: 山羊一「跃」，便跳过了岩石间的缺口。

examples.en: The frog's leap surprised the children watching from the bridge.
examples.zh: 桥上观看的孩子们被青蛙的一「跳」惊到了。

words.enDefinition: a sudden short attack, or a surprise police visit

examples.en: The police raid on the warehouse surprised everyone in the trading quarter.
examples.zh: 警方对仓库的「突查」令商业区所有人都吃了一惊。

examples.en: Villagers dug shelters against air raids during the long war years.
examples.zh: 漫长的战争岁月里，村民挖了防空洞躲避空「袭」。

words.enDefinition: the tenure of a president

examples.en: His presidency is remembered mostly for the new coastal railway.
examples.zh: 人们记住他的「总统任期」，多半是因为那条新建的海岸铁路。

examples.en: She campaigned through every county before winning the union's presidency.
examples.zh: 她跑遍每个郡拉票，最终赢得了学生会的「主席」职位。

words.enDefinition: mechanical device that moves fluid or gas by pressure or suction

examples.en: The old well pump squeaks before it gives any water.
examples.zh: 那口老井的「水泵」先咯吱响几声才出水。

examples.en: The village pump is where neighbours trade news on washing days.
examples.zh: 洗衣的日子里，村里的公用水「泵」旁成了邻居们交换消息的地方。

words.enDefinition: an award for winning a championship or commemorating some other event

examples.en: She keeps her grandmother's Olympic medal in a velvet box.
examples.zh: 她把祖母的奥运「奖牌」收在一个天鹅绒盒子里。

examples.en: He received a medal for carrying two children out of the flood.
examples.zh: 他因从洪水中救出两个孩子而获得了一枚「奖章」。

words.enDefinition: a person or organisation that accepts responsibility for another person

examples.en: The bakery acted as sponsor for the children's football team this season.
examples.zh: 这个赛季，面包房担任了儿童足球队的「赞助人」。

examples.en: Her aunt agreed to be her sponsor for the student visa application.
examples.zh: 姨妈同意做她申请学生签证的「担保人」。

words.enDefinition: (law) a formal accusation against somebody (often in a court of law)

examples.en: The newspaper denied the allegation that it had paid for the interview.
examples.zh: 报社否认了有关它花钱买通采访的「指控」。

examples.en: Police dropped the allegation once the shop owner produced the receipts.
examples.zh: 店主出示收据后，警方撤销了那项「指控」。

words.enDefinition: the selling of goods to consumers; usually in small quantities and not for resale

examples.en: She worked in retail for two summers before opening her own stall.
examples.zh: 自己摆摊前，她做了两个夏天的「零售」工作。

examples.en: The bakery sells bread retail at the counter and wholesale to hotels.
examples.zh: 面包房在柜台「零售」面包，同时也批发给酒店。

words.enDefinition: an indirect suggestion

examples.en: Mom dropped a hint about the new bicycle she wanted for her birthday.
examples.zh: 生日想要新自行车，妈妈早就「暗示」过了。

examples.en: The waiter's polite hint made the loud party take their argument outside.
examples.zh: 服务员礼貌的「暗示」，让那桌吵闹的客人移到了外面。

words.enDefinition: disinclined to become involved

examples.en: Dad was reluctant to lend the car to a brand-new driver.
examples.zh: 爸爸「不情愿」把车借给刚拿驾照的新手。

examples.en: She gave a reluctant yes when the neighbours asked her to sing.
examples.zh: 邻居请她唱一段时，她「勉强」答应了。

words.enDefinition: periodical that is published every month (or 12 issues per year)

examples.en: The village monthly prints the market dates and the church rota.
examples.zh: 村里的「月刊」刊登集市日期和教堂轮值表。

examples.en: He writes a cooking column for the fishing town's monthly.
examples.zh: 他为那座渔镇的「月刊」撰写烹饪专栏。

words.enDefinition: slow movement caused by currents or wind; a general tendency

examples.en: Every October, fallen leaves drift along the canal past the mill.
examples.zh: 每年十月，落叶都顺着运河「漂流」，经过磨坊。

examples.en: The conversation began to drift from the menu prices to old holidays.
examples.zh: 谈话渐渐从菜单价格「漂移」到往年的假期上去。

words.enDefinition: sheltered port where ships can take on or discharge cargo

examples.en: The fishing boats return to the harbour before the evening fog.
examples.zh: 晚雾来临前，渔船都回到了「港口」。

examples.en: We watched the harbour lights come on from the seawall bench.
examples.zh: 我们坐在海堤长椅上，看「港口」的灯一盏盏亮起。

words.enDefinition: transparent optical device used to converge or diverge transmitted light and to form images

examples.en: A grain of sand scratched the camera lens on the beach trip.
examples.zh: 海滩之行让一粒沙子划伤了相机「镜头」。

examples.en: Grandfather cleans his glasses lens with the special cloth from the optician.
examples.zh: 爷爷用眼镜店送的专业布擦拭「镜片」。

words.enDefinition: the exultation of victory

examples.en: Baking the perfect sourdough loaf felt like a small triumph.
examples.zh: 烤出完美的酸面包，感觉像一场小小的「胜利」。

examples.en: The choir's triumph at the regional festival earned them a town concert.
examples.zh: 合唱团在地区艺术节上的「凯旋」为镇上赢得了一场音乐会。

words.enDefinition: evoke or provoke to appear or occur

examples.en: Careless comments about her cooking can provoke the chef for days.
examples.zh: 对她厨艺随口的评论，能「惹恼」厨师好几天。

examples.en: The stray dog bites only when strangers provoke it with sticks.
examples.zh: 那条流浪狗只有在陌生人用棍子「挑衅」时才会咬人。

words.enDefinition: act as a stimulant

examples.en: Coffee at noon stimulates me too much to sleep before midnight.
examples.zh: 中午喝咖啡会让我太「兴奋」，半夜前都睡不着。

examples.en: The mayor hopes the new market will stimulate trade in the old town.
examples.zh: 市长期望新集市能「刺激」老城区的商业。

words.enDefinition: geological formation consisting of an underground enclosure with access from the surface of the ground or from the sea

examples.en: The guide led us into the cave with lanterns and rope.
examples.zh: 向导带着灯笼和绳子，领我们走进那处「洞穴」。

examples.en: The children pretend the gap behind the boathouse is a secret cave.
examples.zh: 孩子们把船屋后面的缝隙当成秘密「山洞」来玩。

words.enDefinition: commissioned military officer in the United States Army or Air Force or Marines who ranks above a lieutenant colonel and below a brigadier general

examples.en: The colonel inspected the mess hall before the annual dinner.
examples.zh: 年度晚宴前，「上校」视察了官兵食堂。

examples.en: Our neighbour, a retired colonel, still polishes his old medals every spring.
examples.zh: 我们那位退休「上校」邻居，每年春天仍会把旧勋章擦亮。

words.enDefinition: relating to or characteristic of diplomacy

examples.en: His diplomatic reply kept the family dinner from turning into a quarrel.
examples.zh: 他一番圆融「得体的」回应，避免家宴变成争吵。

examples.en: She received diplomatic training before posting abroad, so complaints never rattle her.
examples.zh: 她外派前受过「外交」训练，所以投诉从不让她慌乱。

words.enDefinition: member of the United States Marine Corps

examples.en: The marine carried his wounded friend down the hill to the medic.
examples.zh: 那名「海军陆战队士兵」背着受伤的战友下山找军医。

examples.en: Marines from the local base marched in the town's parade every summer.
examples.zh: 每年夏天，当地基地的「海军陆战队士兵」都会参加镇上的游行。

words.enDefinition: a pipe or channel that carries away water or waste liquid

examples.en: Hair clogged the bathroom drain again, so we bought a wire snake.
examples.zh: 浴室「下水道」又被头发堵了，我们只好买了根通渠钢丝。

examples.en: The kitchen drain gurgles whenever the washing machine empties upstairs.
examples.zh: 楼上洗衣机排水时，厨房「下水管」就咕噜咕噜响。

words.enDefinition: freedom of choice

examples.en: Retirement finally gave him the liberty to fish every morning.
examples.zh: 退休终于让他有了每天早晨垂钓的「自由」。

examples.en: The dogs enjoy the liberty of the whole garden now that the fence is fixed.
examples.zh: 栅栏修好后，狗狗们可以在整个花园里「自由」撒欢了。

words.enDefinition: to carry out a plan, order, or piece of work

examples.en: The team executed the fire-drill plan calmly when the alarm sounded.
examples.zh: 警报响起时，全队镇定地「执行」了消防演练方案。

examples.en: A good recipe works only if you execute each step carefully.
examples.zh: 只有认真「执行」每个步骤，好菜谱才能做出好菜。

words.enDefinition: very impressive or dramatic

examples.en: The fireworks over the lake were spectacular, even from the far shore.
examples.zh: 湖上的焰火十分「壮观」，隔着湖对岸都看得清。

examples.en: Their spectacular comeback in the final ten minutes stunned the crowd.
examples.zh: 最后十分钟「精彩的」绝地反击让观众都惊呆了。

words.enDefinition: person who lacks good judgment

examples.en: Only a fool would leave the tent open in bear country.
examples.zh: 在有熊出没的地方不关帐篷，只有「傻瓜」才干得出来。

examples.en: He played the fool at the wedding to keep the nervous couple laughing.
examples.zh: 他在婚礼上扮「小丑」逗乐，让紧张的新人笑个不停。

words.enDefinition: device that activates or releases or causes something to happen

examples.en: Never put your finger on the trigger until you mean to shoot.
examples.zh: 没打算开枪之前，手指绝不要碰「扳机」。

examples.en: Pulling the trigger of the starter pistol set the runners off.
examples.zh: 发令枪的「扳机」一扣，选手们便冲了出去。

words.enDefinition: person serving a sentence in a jail or prison

examples.en: The convict repairs bicycles in the prison workshop three days a week.
examples.zh: 那名「囚犯」每周三天在监狱工坊里修自行车。

examples.en: Guards escorted the convict to the courthouse under heavy rain.
examples.zh: 大雨中，狱警押送「囚犯」前往法院。

words.enDefinition: middle way between two extremes

examples.en: After an hour of arguing, we reached a compromise on paint colours.
examples.zh: 争论一小时后，我们就油漆颜色达成了「折中」。

examples.en: Meeting at the halfway cafe was a fair compromise for both families.
examples.zh: 在中途的咖啡馆碰面，对两家来说是个公平的「妥协方案」。

words.enDefinition: an increase or improvement that helps something develop

examples.en: The kind review gave the little bookshop a real boost.
examples.zh: 那则善意的书评给这家小书店带来了实实在在的「提振」。

examples.en: A cup of sweet tea gave him the boost he needed to finish the climb.
examples.zh: 一杯甜茶给了他爬完全程所需的「助力」。

words.enDefinition: document listing the alternatives that is used in voting

examples.en: Voters marked the ballot in the wooden booth behind the curtain.
examples.zh: 选民在帘子后的木隔间里填写「选票」。

examples.en: The club counts every ballot twice before announcing the new secretary.
examples.zh: 宣布新秘书人选前，俱乐部会把每张「选票」数两遍。

words.enDefinition: a room or hall at the entrance of a building

examples.en: The hotel lobby smelled of fresh coffee and lemon polish.
examples.zh: 酒店「大堂」里飘着现磨咖啡和柠檬抛光剂的气味。

examples.en: Residents are repainting the apartment lobby in pale blue this weekend.
examples.zh: 这个周末，住户们要把公寓「门厅」重新刷成淡蓝色。

words.enDefinition: dishonest or illegal behaviour by people in power

examples.en: The mayor's corruption scandal emptied the council chamber in a single week.
examples.zh: 市长的「贪腐」丑闻让市议会在一周内人去楼空。

examples.en: Voters punish corruption most harshly when it touches the school budget.
examples.zh: 当「腐败」触及学校预算时，选民的惩罚最为严厉。

words.enDefinition: an overwhelming feeling of fear and anxiety

examples.en: She felt a brief panic when the plane door wouldn't budge.
examples.zh: 飞机门推不动的那一刻，她心中闪过一丝「恐慌」。

examples.en: Don't panic if the dog jumps into the pool after you.
examples.zh: 狗跳进泳池追你时，「别慌」。

words.enDefinition: in an official role

examples.en: The bridge officially opens to traffic on the first of May.
examples.zh: 大桥将于五月一日「正式」通车。

examples.en: She is officially the treasurer, though her brother keeps the books.
examples.zh: 「名义上」她是财务主管，其实账目由她弟弟记。

words.enDefinition: public act of violence by an unruly mob

examples.en: Police contained the riot outside the stadium without serious injuries.
examples.zh: 警方在体育场外控制住了「暴乱」，没有造成重伤。

examples.en: The food riot of the hungry winter is still remembered by elders.
examples.zh: 老人们仍记得饥荒那年冬天爆发的食物「骚乱」。

words.enDefinition: give instructions or directions for some task

examples.en: The optician instructed me to wear the new glasses only at night.
examples.zh: 配镜师「嘱咐」我夜间才戴这副新眼镜。

examples.en: Grandmother instructed the whole family on how to fold the dumplings properly.
examples.zh: 奶奶「教」全家人怎么把饺子包得地道。

words.enDefinition: genre of popular music that originated in New Orleans around 1900 and developed through increasingly complex styles

examples.en: The harbour cafe plays live jazz on the first Friday of each month.
examples.zh: 海港咖啡馆每月第一个周五都有现场「爵士乐」。

examples.en: Grandfather's old jazz records filled the parlour every Sunday afternoon.
examples.zh: 每周日下午，「爵士乐」的旧唱片声充满了客厅。

words.enDefinition: admit (to a wrongdoing)

examples.en: The baker finally conceded that the new oven bakes unevenly.
examples.zh: 面包师傅最终「承认」新烤箱烤得不均匀。

examples.en: Down two goals, the home side conceded the match with grace.
examples.zh: 主队落后两球，体面地「认输」了。

words.enDefinition: state of conflict between persons

examples.en: The two parades clash every year on the same street.
examples.zh: 两支游行队伍每年都会在同一条街上「冲突」。

examples.en: Green and orange clash badly in that little sitting room.
examples.zh: 绿色和橙色在那间小客厅里「很不搭」。

words.enDefinition: to make information known to the public

examples.en: The seller must disclose the roof damage before signing the contract.
examples.zh: 签合同前，卖方必须「披露」屋顶的损坏情况。

examples.en: She refused to disclose where the clinic gets its donated supplies.
examples.zh: 她拒绝「透露」诊所捐赠物资的来源。

words.enDefinition: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions; inclined to react violently; fervid

examples.en: A fierce storm bent the flagpole but spared the market stalls.
examples.zh: 一场「猛烈的」风暴吹弯了旗杆，市场摊位却安然无恙。

examples.en: Competition between the two fish-and-chip shops on the pier is fierce.
examples.zh: 码头上两家炸鱼薯条店的竞争非常「激烈」。

words.enDefinition: prepare for publication or presentation by correcting, revising, or adapting

examples.en: She edits the village newsletter from her kitchen table every Thursday.
examples.zh: 每周四，她都在自家餐桌前「编辑」村刊。

examples.en: Edit the essay once for grammar and once for tone.
examples.zh: 作文要「修改」两遍：一遍查语法，一遍调语气。

words.enDefinition: state of extreme anger

examples.en: Grandfather's quiet rage showed only in the way he folded the newspaper.
examples.zh: 爷爷压着的「怒气」，只从他折报纸的动作里露出来。

examples.en: The storm raged along the coast all night, tearing shutters loose.
examples.zh: 风暴「肆虐」海岸一整夜，把百叶窗都撕落了。

words.enDefinition: the place where an event or meeting is held

examples.en: The couple finally chose the lighthouse lawn as their wedding venue.
examples.zh: 这对新人最终选定灯塔草坪作为婚礼「场地」。

examples.en: The touring band switched venues after the roof of the hall leaked.
examples.zh: 礼堂屋顶漏水后，巡演乐队更换了演出「场馆」。

words.enDefinition: with respect to sexuality

examples.en: Doctors explained that the infection can be transmitted sexually as well as through blood.
examples.zh: 医生解释说，这种感染既可通过血液传播，也可通过「性接触」传播。

examples.en: The court heard that the manager had harassed staff sexually for months.
examples.zh: 法庭审理得知，该经理数月来一直对员工进行「性骚扰」。

words.enDefinition: intended to last only for a short time until something permanent exists

examples.en: The interim manager runs the bakery until the owners hire someone permanent.
examples.zh: 「临时的」经理先打理面包房，直到店主聘到长期人选。

examples.en: We signed an interim lease for the flat while the new one is painted.
examples.zh: 新公寓粉刷期间，我们先签了「临时的」租房合同。

words.enDefinition: the head of a government; a prime minister

examples.en: The premier opened the new harbour tunnel with a ribbon ceremony.
examples.zh: 「总理」以剪彩仪式为新海港隧道揭幕。

examples.en: Reporters asked the premier about ferry prices at the village fair.
examples.zh: 乡村集市上，记者们向「总理」询问轮渡票价。

words.enDefinition: personnel that are sacrificed (e.g., surrendered or lost in order to gain an objective)

examples.en: Parents often make the sacrifice of sleep during a baby's first year.
examples.zh: 孩子出生头一年，父母常在睡眠上作出「牺牲」。

examples.en: The team's sacrifice of a holiday weekend brought the harvest in on time.
examples.zh: 全队「牺牲」一个假期周末，及时收完了庄稼。

words.enDefinition: any vehicle self-propelled by a rocket engine

examples.en: The children launched a toy rocket from the top of the hay barn.
examples.zh: 孩子们从干草棚顶发射了一枚玩具「火箭」。

examples.en: A rocket's red flare announced the start of the regatta.
examples.zh: 「火箭」的红光一闪，帆船赛开始了。

words.enDefinition: become more focus on an area of activity or field of study

examples.en: This little shop specializes in cheeses from the neighbouring valleys.
examples.zh: 这家小店「专门经营」邻谷各地出产的奶酪。

examples.en: After culinary school, she decided to specialize in pastry work.
examples.zh: 烹饪学校毕业后，她决定「专攻」甜点制作。

words.enDefinition: (law) the findings of a jury on issues of fact submitted to it for decision; can be used in formulating a judgment

examples.en: The jury reached its verdict after only two hours of discussion.
examples.zh: 陪审团讨论了仅仅两小时便作出「裁决」。

examples.en: Villagers awaited the doctor's verdict on the injured shepherd anxiously.
examples.zh: 村民们焦急地等待医生对受伤牧羊人的「判断」。

words.enDefinition: protected from a disease or an unwelcome influence

examples.en: After the vaccination, most children become immune to measles for life.
examples.zh: 接种疫苗后，大多数孩子终生对麻疹「免疫」。

examples.en: Years of commuting have made him almost immune to the noise of the city.
examples.zh: 多年的通勤让他对城市噪音几乎「无感」了。

words.enDefinition: large gathering of people intended to arouse enthusiasm

examples.en: Thousands attended the peace rally in the market square on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，数千人参加了集市广场上的和平「集会」。

examples.en: Candidates held their final rally by the harbour the night before the vote.
examples.zh: 投票前夜，候选人在港口边举行了最后一场「竞选集会」。

words.enDefinition: the first public appearance of someone or something

examples.en: The young pianist's debut at the town hall sold out in a week.
examples.zh: 年轻钢琴家的「首演」门票一周内在镇礼堂售罄。

examples.en: Her debut as a director surprised everyone who knew her as a quiet editor.
examples.zh: 她作为导演的「首秀」让所有认识她这个安静编辑的人吃了一惊。

words.enDefinition: an instrument with a handle and a flexible lash that is used for whipping

examples.en: The rider cracked his whip gently above the pony's back, never touching it.
examples.zh: 骑手在马背上空轻甩「马鞭」，从不碰到小马。

examples.en: Grandfather still keeps the leather whip from his days as a stagecoach guard.
examples.zh: 爷爷仍留着当年当驿车护卫时用的皮「鞭子」。

words.enDefinition: look over carefully

examples.en: The building inspector will inspect the loft conversion next Tuesday.
examples.zh: 建筑检查员下周二将「查验」阁楼改造工程。

examples.en: Buyers inspected the used tractor closely before negotiating the price.
examples.zh: 买家仔细「检查」了二手拖拉机，才开始议价。

words.enDefinition: correctly, or for good reasons

examples.en: The umpire rightly stopped the match when lightning appeared over the hills.
examples.zh: 山那边出现闪电时，裁判「正确地」中止了比赛。

examples.en: Parents rightly expect the bus company to answer for the delay.
examples.zh: 家长们「理所当然地」要求公交公司为延误负责。

words.enDefinition: by or with respect to society

examples.en: The new cafe is socially important as the only place neighbours can meet.
examples.zh: 这家新咖啡馆「在社交上」很重要，是邻居们唯一能碰头的地方。

examples.en: She became socially active in the village after joining the residents' committee.
examples.zh: 加入居民委员会后，她「在社区社交上」活跃起来。

words.enDefinition: a stop or pause

examples.en: Traffic came to a sudden halt when the sheep crossed the road.
examples.zh: 羊群过马路时，车流骤然「停住」。

examples.en: The builder called a halt to the work until the rain eased.
examples.zh: 工头叫「停」了施工，等雨势变小再说。

words.enDefinition: an outbuilding with a single story; used for shelter or storage

examples.en: Grandfather keeps his seedling trays in the potting shed behind the wall.
examples.zh: 爷爷把育苗盘放在墙后的「工具棚」里。

examples.en: The storm lifted the tin roof right off the garden shed.
examples.zh: 风暴把花园「棚屋」的铁皮顶整个掀走了。

words.enDefinition: a public sale where items go to the highest bidder

examples.en: The farm equipment auction drew buyers from three different counties.
examples.zh: 农机「拍卖会」吸引了三个郡的买家。

examples.en: She bid carefully at the furniture auction and got the oak dresser.
examples.zh: 她在家具「拍卖」会上谨慎出价，拍得了那张橡木五斗柜。

words.enDefinition: connected with or belonging to or used in a navy

examples.en: The naval museum displays uniforms and charts from the harbour's past.
examples.zh: 这座「海军」博物馆陈列着港口往日的制服与海图。

examples.en: The town's naval history comes alive in the veterans' storytelling evenings.
examples.zh: 老兵们讲故事的那几晚，小镇的「海军」历史变得鲜活起来。

words.zhGloss: （就重大政治或社会问题进行的）全民公决
words.enDefinition: legislative act is referred for final approval to a popular vote by the electorate
acceptedZhAnswers: （就重大政治或社会问题进行的）全民公决

examples.en: The village voted in a referendum to keep the old stone bridge.
examples.zh: 全村在「公投」中决定保留那座古老石桥。

examples.en: A referendum on the market hours divided the shopkeepers down the middle.
examples.zh: 关于集市营业时间的「全民公决」让店主们分成两派。

words.enDefinition: a moment; an exact point in time

examples.en: In an instant, the cat was through the open window and gone.
examples.zh: 「一瞬间」，猫就钻出敞开的窗户跑没了影。

examples.en: At the instant the clock struck twelve, the lights in the hall failed.
examples.zh: 时钟敲响十二点的那一「刹那」，大厅的灯全灭了。

words.enDefinition: in accordance with truth or fact or reality

examples.en: The shopkeeper apologized genuinely and refunded both tickets without argument.
examples.zh: 店主「真诚地」道歉，二话不说退了两张票。

examples.en: He was genuinely surprised to see his old teacher at the concert.
examples.zh: 在音乐会上遇见旧日的老师，他是「真心」感到惊讶。

words.enDefinition: spanning or extending throughout the entire world

examples.en: The soup recipe from our village is now famous worldwide.
examples.zh: 我们村的那道汤菜如今「闻名全世界」。

examples.en: Fans worldwide followed the fishing boat rescue on the news.
examples.zh: 全「世界」的新闻观众都在关注那艘渔船的救援。

words.enDefinition: lessen the strength of

examples.en: Skipping meals can weaken you before a long shift at the hospital.
examples.zh: 长时间医院值班前不吃饭，会让你的体力「变弱」。

examples.en: The old rope weakened after years in the sun and finally snapped.
examples.zh: 旧绳子晒了多年早已「不结实」，最后还是断了。

words.enDefinition: bold challenge

examples.en: The quiet shepherd avoided confrontation by moving his flock to another field.
examples.zh: 沉默的牧羊人把羊群赶到另一块地里，避免了「对峙」。

examples.en: The confrontation between the two taxi queues ended with shared laughs.
examples.zh: 两队出租车主的「争执」最后以一同大笑收场。

words.enDefinition: with few mistakes

examples.en: The surveyor measured the boundary accurately enough to satisfy both farms.
examples.zh: 测量员把地界量得足够「准确」，双方农场都认可。

examples.en: She can recall prices accurately even years after the shop closed.
examples.zh: 店铺关门多年后，她仍能「准确地」记得各种价钱。

words.enDefinition: diplomat of the highest rank; accredited as representative from one country to another

examples.en: The ambassador opened the cultural week with a speech about trade.
examples.zh: 「大使」以一场关于贸易的演讲为文化周揭幕。

examples.en: The retiring ambassador plans to write a book about the harbour towns.
examples.zh: 即将卸任的「大使」打算写一本关于海港小镇的书。

words.enDefinition: steep and rapid fall

examples.en: The sudden plunge in ferry bookings left the harbour cafe half empty.
examples.zh: 轮渡订票量「骤降」，港口咖啡馆冷清了一半。

examples.en: The stock market plunge wiped out the fishing fleet expansion plans.
examples.zh: 市场「暴跌」让渔船队扩建计划泡了汤。

words.enDefinition: an amount that is more than necessary or allowed

examples.en: Cut away any excess dough before crimping the pie edges.
examples.zh: 捏派皮花边前，先切掉「多余的」面团。

examples.en: The council fined the factory for excess noise after ten at night.
examples.zh: 工厂夜里十点后噪音「超标」，被市政罚款。

words.enDefinition: by law; conforming to the law

examples.en: You must be legally registered to run a market stall here.
examples.zh: 在这里摆摊必须「依法」登记。

examples.en: The charity makes sure that every donation is legally documented.
examples.zh: 慈善机构确保每笔捐款都有「合法的」书面记录。

words.enDefinition: on your own; without outside help

examples.en: The auditor works independently of the very shops he inspects.
examples.zh: 审计员「独立于」他所检查的店铺开展工作。

examples.en: My daughter booked the ferry tickets independently for the first time.
examples.zh: 女儿第一次「独立」订好了轮渡票。

words.enDefinition: an expensive vessel propelled by sail or power and used for cruising or racing

examples.en: The doctor's yacht anchored beside the fishermen's boats in the bay.
examples.zh: 医生的「游艇」在港湾里就停在渔船旁边。

examples.en: They spent their honeymoon sailing a small yacht along the coast.
examples.zh: 他们蜜月时驾着一艘小型「游艇」沿海岸航行。

words.enDefinition: cry or shout of approval

examples.en: A great cheer went up when the raft crossed the finish line.
examples.zh: 木筏冲过终点线时，人群中爆发出一阵「欢呼」。

examples.en: The team heard the cheer of the whole village from the field.
examples.zh: 球队在场地上听到了全村人的「喝彩」。

words.enDefinition: dissenting clique

examples.en: A faction within the club wants the market moved to Saturdays.
examples.zh: 俱乐部内部有一「派」想把集市挪到周六。

examples.en: The two factions finally shared the hall for alternating concert nights.
examples.zh: 两「派」最终共用礼堂，轮流举办音乐会之夜。

words.enDefinition: writer who reports and analyzes events of the day

examples.en: The radio commentator described the storm damage with remarkable calm.
examples.zh: 电台「评论员」异常镇定地播报了风暴灾情。

examples.en: Our favourite television commentator retires after this season of matches.
examples.zh: 我们最爱的电视「解说员」将在本赛季后退休。

words.enDefinition: in an emotional manner

examples.en: Talking about the flood still affects her emotionally after two years.
examples.zh: 两年过去，谈起那场洪水，她在「情绪上」仍会受触动。

examples.en: The reunion film left everyone emotionally exhausted but quietly happy.
examples.zh: 那部重逢题材的影片让大家「情绪上」疲惫，却又暗自欣喜。

words.zhGloss: 乘船巡游；海上度假之旅
words.enDefinition: an ocean trip taken for pleasure

examples.en: They celebrated their anniversary with a cruise among the islands.
examples.zh: 他们以一场「乘船巡游」庆祝结婚周年，途中遍游群岛。

examples.en: The harbour cruise passes the lighthouse and the old canning factory.
examples.zh: 港口「巡游」航线经过灯塔和旧罐头厂。

words.enDefinition: in an important way or to an important degree

examples.en: More importantly, the ferry now runs even when the fog rolls in.
examples.zh: 更「重要的是」，如今即使起雾轮渡也照开。

examples.en: She finished the report on time and, importantly, without any errors.
examples.zh: 她按时完成了报告，而且「重要的」是没有出错。

words.enDefinition: with neatness

examples.en: Grandmother stacks the linens neatly by shelf and by season.
examples.zh: 奶奶把床单桌布按柜格和季节「整整齐齐地」码好。

examples.en: He writes his market lists neatly in blue ink every morning.
examples.zh: 他每天早上都用蓝墨水把采购单写得「工工整整」。

words.enDefinition: (of a person) attractively thin; also small in amount

examples.en: The slim young shepherd moved surprisingly fast across the scree.
examples.zh: 那位「苗条的」年轻牧羊人在碎石坡上跑得出奇地快。

examples.en: She kept slim by walking the long way home every evening.
examples.zh: 她每晚绕远路走回家，一直保持「纤细」的身材。

words.enDefinition: gases ejected from an engine as waste products

examples.en: The truck's exhaust rattles loose every time we cross the cattle grid.
examples.zh: 每次过牛栏格栅，卡车的「排气管」都会哐当哐当地晃。

examples.en: Rain and exhaust fumes hung over the bus station at dusk.
examples.zh: 黄昏的公交站上空笼罩着雨水和「尾气」。

words.enDefinition: an explosion or a sudden strong gust of air

examples.en: The quarry blast at noon shook windows two villages away.
examples.zh: 正午采石场的「爆破」震得两个村子外都窗响。

examples.en: A sudden blast of cold air swept through the open market door.
examples.zh: 一股「冷风」突然从敞开的市场门里灌了进来。

words.enDefinition: during or for the length of one night

examples.en: The sauce improves overnight in the fridge, so make it a day ahead.
examples.zh: 酱汁在冰箱里放「一夜」会更入味，所以提前一天做好。

examples.en: We stayed overnight at the harbour inn before catching the early ferry.
examples.zh: 赶早班轮渡前，我们在港口客栈「过夜」。

words.enDefinition: (military) withdrawal of troops to a more favorable position to escape the enemy's superior forces or after a defeat

examples.en: The army's retreat across the frozen river saved most of the wounded.
examples.zh: 部队沿冰冻的河流「撤退」，保住了大部分伤员。

examples.en: Trumpets signalled the retreat as the sun sank behind the ridge.
examples.zh: 太阳落到山脊后，号角吹响了「撤退」的信号。

words.enDefinition: small but noticeable trace of some quality that might become stronger

examples.en: One spark from the grinder set the straw stack smouldering.
examples.zh: 砂轮迸出的一粒「火星」，让草垛阴燃了起来。

examples.en: A single kind comment at the bus stop can spark a lifelong friendship.
examples.zh: 公交站上一句善意的话，能「点燃」一生的友谊。

words.enDefinition: quantity much larger than is needed

examples.en: We sell the surplus eggs from the garden gate every weekend.
examples.zh: 每个周末，我们都在院门口卖掉「多余的」鸡蛋。

examples.en: The harvest left the co-op with a surplus of pickled cabbage.
examples.zh: 丰收让合作社积攒下「剩余的」腌白菜。

words.enDefinition: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of

examples.en: Potholes on the shortcut frustrate delivery drivers every single winter.
examples.zh: 近路上的坑洼年年都让送货司机「头疼」。

examples.en: The locked gate frustrated our plans for a moonlight picnic.
examples.zh: 上了锁的大门让我们的月夜野餐计划「落了空」。

words.enDefinition: person who comes from a foreign country; someone who does not owe allegiance to your country

examples.en: As the only foreigner in the village, she gets invited to every dinner.
examples.zh: 作为村里唯一的「外国人」，每一顿饭局她都会被邀请。

examples.en: The market trader switched to gestures when the foreigner looked puzzled.
examples.zh: 见「外国」游客一脸困惑，市场摊主便改用手势。

words.enDefinition: an official engaged in international negotiations

examples.en: The veteran diplomat settled the border dispute over one long dinner.
examples.zh: 那位经验丰富的「外交官」一顿长长的晚餐就化解了边界争端。

examples.en: The retired diplomat now teaches schoolchildren how to greet guests politely.
examples.zh: 退休的「外交官」如今教小学生如何礼貌迎宾。

words.enDefinition: reestablish on a new, usually improved, basis or make new or like new

examples.en: You can renew your library ticket at the desk or by phone.
examples.zh: 你可以在服务台或通过电话「续办」图书证。

examples.en: The couple renewed their wedding vows at the little chapel by the sea.
examples.zh: 这对夫妇在海边的小教堂「重申」了结婚誓言。

words.enDefinition: quick to notice and respond to something; watchful

examples.en: Stay alert when the bus stops, because pickpockets work the evening routes.
examples.zh: 公交停靠时要保持「警惕」，小偷专挑晚间线路下手。

examples.en: The nurse on night duty stays alert with short walks between rounds.
examples.zh: 夜班护士在查房间隙短暂走动，让自己保持「清醒警觉」。

words.enDefinition: in a beautiful manner

examples.en: The bride's younger sister sang beautifully at the harbour ceremony.
examples.zh: 新娘的妹妹在海港婚礼上唱得「动听极了」。

examples.en: The old clock was beautifully restored by the jeweller on the square.
examples.zh: 广场上那位珠宝匠把老钟修复得「精美漂亮」。

words.enDefinition: an article in a newspaper giving the editor's opinion

examples.en: The paper's editorial praised the volunteers who cleaned the beach.
examples.zh: 报纸的「社论」称赞了清理海滩的志愿者。

examples.en: She wrote the editorial defending the market traders after the fire.
examples.zh: 火灾后，她撰写「社论」为集市摊主辩护。

words.enDefinition: to give up control, possession, or resistance to someone else

examples.en: The garrison finally chose to surrender when the food ran out.
examples.zh: 粮食耗尽时，守军最终选择「投降」。

examples.en: He had to surrender his keys at the front desk of the hostel.
examples.zh: 在青年旅舍前台，他不得不「交出」钥匙。

words.enDefinition: someone who pursues a study or sport as a pastime

examples.en: The amateur choir rehearses in the school hall every Thursday.
examples.zh: 这支「业余」合唱团每周四在学校礼堂排练。

examples.en: As an amateur gardener, she grows prize pumpkins purely for fun.
examples.zh: 作为「业余」园丁，她种获奖南瓜纯粹为了好玩。

words.enDefinition: a pointed device on a rider's heel used to urge a horse on

examples.en: The cowboy's silver spurs jingled as he crossed the saloon floor.
examples.zh: 牛仔穿过酒馆地板时，银「马刺」叮当作响。

examples.en: Riders remove their spurs before entering the stable, by tradition.
examples.zh: 按传统，骑手进马厩前要先摘下「马刺」。

words.enDefinition: the state of being sent away from one's home country; also a person in that state

examples.en: The poet spent twenty years in exile writing about his distant coast.
examples.zh: 「流亡」二十年间，诗人笔耕不辍，写的都是远方的海岸。

examples.en: The family returned from exile once the new government granted amnesty.
examples.zh: 新政府宣布大赦后，这家人结束了「流放」生涯归来。

words.enDefinition: conduct a prosecution in a court of law

examples.en: The council decided to prosecute the factory for dumping waste in the river.
examples.zh: 市政决定就该厂向河中倾倒废物提起「起诉」。

examples.en: Lawyers prosecuted the case for months before the verdict came.
examples.zh: 律师们「起诉」此案数月，判决才下来。

words.enDefinition: an accidental hole that allows something (fluid or light etc.) to enter or escape

examples.en: The plumber found the leak behind the washing machine in ten minutes.
examples.zh: 水管工十分钟就找到了洗衣机后面的「漏水点」。

examples.en: A slow leak in the gas line forced the school to close early.
examples.zh: 煤气管道的缓慢「泄漏」迫使学校提前放学。

words.enDefinition: a solemn promise or undertaking

examples.en: The bridesmaids made a pledge to keep the wedding venue a surprise.
examples.zh: 伴娘们「许下承诺」，要对婚礼场地保密到底。

examples.en: Members signed the club's pledge to look after the allotment paths.
examples.zh: 会员们签署了俱乐部的「承诺书」，保证照看好园圃小路。

words.enDefinition: careful to avoid risks or mistakes; showing careful forethought

examples.en: Be cautious about phone calls asking for your bank details.
examples.zh: 凡是索要银行信息的电话，都要「谨慎」对待。

examples.en: The cautious driver checks the tyres twice before a mountain trip.
examples.zh: 「谨慎的」司机出发上山前，会把轮胎检查两遍。

words.enDefinition: something that is an indulgence rather than a necessity

examples.en: Hot showers on the trail felt like pure luxury after a week.
examples.zh: 走了一周山路后，热水淋浴简直是纯粹的「奢侈享受」。

examples.en: For them, a whole weekend off is a luxury they rarely afford.
examples.zh: 对他们来说，整个周末休假是一种难得的「奢侈」。

words.enDefinition: causing to feel shame or chagrin or vexation

examples.en: The karaoke machine broke at the most embarrassing moment of the party.
examples.zh: 卡拉OK机恰好在派对最「尴尬的」时刻坏了。

examples.en: It was embarrassing to forget the mayor's name twice at the fair.
examples.zh: 在集市上两次忘记市长的名字，真是「令人尴尬」。

words.enDefinition: unbearable physical pain

examples.en: Waiting for exam results is a slow torture for the whole family.
examples.zh: 等待考试成绩对全家人来说是一种缓慢的「折磨」。

examples.en: Historians documented the torture methods once used in the old prison.
examples.zh: 历史学家记录了旧监狱曾使用的「酷刑」手段。

words.enDefinition: in an adequate manner or to an adequate degree

examples.en: The old bridge was not adequately supported, so lorries now detour.
examples.zh: 老桥的支撑「不够牢固」，如今货车都绕行。

examples.en: Make sure the tent is adequately pegged before the night wind rises.
examples.zh: 夜风起来之前，务必把帐篷「充分地」固定好。

words.enDefinition: with efficiency; in an efficient manner

examples.en: The new dishwasher cleans a full load efficiently in half an hour.
examples.zh: 新洗碗机半小时就能「高效地」洗完一整批餐具。

examples.en: She organises the harvest rota efficiently, with everyone's name and day.
examples.zh: 她把收割轮值表安排得「井井有条」，人名和日期一目了然。

words.enDefinition: in collaboration or cooperation

examples.en: The two families jointly funded the new playground behind the church.
examples.zh: 两家人「共同」出资，在教堂后面建了新游乐场。

examples.en: The neighbours jointly hired a lawyer to challenge the road plan.
examples.zh: 邻居们「联合」聘请律师，对修路方案提出异议。

words.enDefinition: not in a forthright manner

examples.en: The manager hinted only indirectly that overtime would be needed on Friday.
examples.zh: 经理只是「间接地」暗示周五需要加班。

examples.en: Smoke from the bonfire reached us indirectly through the open windows.
examples.zh: 篝火的烟经由敞开的窗户「间接」飘到了我们这里。

words.enDefinition: in a strange manner

examples.en: The old dog looked strangely at the empty bowl before walking away.
examples.zh: 老狗「奇怪地」盯着空食盆看了一会儿才走开。

examples.en: Strangely enough, the baker's bread rose better on cloudy days.
examples.zh: 说来也「怪」，阴天时面包师傅的面团发得更好。

words.enDefinition: any piece of furniture or decorative object or the like produced in a former period and valuable because of its beauty or rarity

examples.en: The dealer identified the writing desk as a genuine antique from 1790.
examples.zh: 古董商鉴定这张写字台是 1790 年的「真古董」。

examples.en: She hunts for antique door handles at every flea market in the region.
examples.zh: 她在区内每个跳蚤市场搜寻「古董」门把手。

words.enDefinition: at every point

examples.en: The old mill wheel turned continuously from spring until the canal froze.
examples.zh: 从开春到运河封冻，老磨坊的水轮一直「不停地」转。

examples.en: Rain fell continuously for three days, and the river crept over its banks.
examples.zh: 雨连下了三天，「持续不断」，河水慢慢漫过了堤岸。

words.enDefinition: filled with the emotional impact of overwhelming surprise or shock

examples.en: The judges were amazed by the ten-year-old's harvest loaf.
examples.zh: 评委对那个十岁孩子的丰收面包感到「惊叹」。

examples.en: Amazed tourists photographed the double rainbow over the fishing pier.
examples.zh: 「惊叹不已的」游客纷纷拍下渔码头上空的双彩虹。

words.enDefinition: in a way that was not expected

examples.en: The ferry arrived unexpectedly early, so we caught the afternoon train.
examples.zh: 轮渡「出乎意料地」提前到了，我们赶上了下午的火车。

examples.en: My quiet neighbour unexpectedly won the regional pie contest this year.
examples.zh: 我那位安静的邻居今年「意外地」赢得了地区派大赛。

words.enDefinition: passage selected from a larger work

examples.en: The teacher read an excerpt from the village legend to the class.
examples.zh: 老师给全班朗读了村中传说的一则「节选」。

examples.en: The programme includes an excerpt from the choir's winning performance.
examples.zh: 节目单里包含合唱团获奖演出的一段「选段」。

words.enDefinition: in a manner differing from the usual or expected

examples.en: The goat followed us curiously from gate to gate all afternoon.
examples.zh: 整个下午，那只山羊都「好奇地」跟着我们，从一道门跟到另一道门。

examples.en: Curiously, the coldest room in the inn is the one beside the kitchen.
examples.zh: 说来「奇怪」，客栈里最冷的房间偏偏在厨房旁边。

words.enDefinition: in secrecy; not openly

examples.en: The children secretly buried a time capsule under the old pear tree.
examples.zh: 孩子们「偷偷地」在老梨树下埋了一个时间胶囊。

examples.en: She secretly practised the accordion at night for the winter concert.
examples.zh: 为了冬季音乐会，她夜里「悄悄地」练习手风琴。

words.enDefinition: with pride; in a proud manner

examples.en: The coach proudly watched her rowing team cross the finish first.
examples.zh: 教练「自豪地」看着自己的赛艇队率先冲过终点。

examples.en: He proudly showed us the barn he rebuilt with his own hands.
examples.zh: 他「骄傲地」向我们展示亲手重建的谷仓。

words.enDefinition: with respect to moral principles

examples.en: Grandfather believes it is morally wrong to waste good bread.
examples.zh: 爷爷认为浪费好面包「在道德上」是错误的。

examples.en: The committee debated whether the fee increase was morally defensible.
examples.zh: 委员会讨论这次收费上调「在道义上」是否站得住脚。

words.enDefinition: in a polite manner

examples.en: The children politely thanked the bus driver before getting off.
examples.zh: 孩子们下车前「有礼貌地」向司机道了谢。

examples.en: She politely asked the loud group to move their picnic blanket.
examples.zh: 她「客气地」请那群吵闹的人挪一下野餐垫。

words.enDefinition: with brightness

examples.en: The harbour lamps shone brightly through the thin evening mist.
examples.zh: 港湾的灯火透过薄暮「明亮地」闪耀着。

examples.en: The stalls were painted brightly for the spring fair this year.
examples.zh: 今年春季集市，摊位都刷得「色彩鲜艳」。

words.enDefinition: in an illegal manner

examples.en: The council fined the campsite because it parked caravans illegally near the cliff.
examples.zh: 因「违规」把大篷车停在悬崖附近，露营地被市政罚款。

examples.en: They discovered that the old extension had been built illegally without permits.
examples.zh: 他们发现那间旧扩建房当年是「非法」建造、没有许可证的。

words.enDefinition: in an anxiously nervous manner

examples.en: The puppy waited nervously by the door during its first thunderstorm.
examples.zh: 第一次遇上雷暴，小狗「紧张地」守在门边。

examples.en: She checked the oven nervously every five minutes before the judges arrived.
examples.zh: 评委到来前，她每五分钟就「不安地」查看一次烤箱。

words.enDefinition: annoy continually or chronically

examples.en: Residents asked the council to stop the calls that harass elderly people at dinner.
examples.zh: 居民们请求市政制止那些在晚餐时间「骚扰」老人的电话。

examples.en: The boss was fined for trying to harass workers into unpaid weekend shifts.
examples.zh: 老板因不断「骚扰」员工、强要周末无偿加班而被罚款。

words.enDefinition: using aggressive methods to support a cause

examples.en: The militant faction refused any compromise with the ferry company.
examples.zh: 那一「好战的」派系拒绝与轮渡公司作任何妥协。

examples.en: His militant defence of the harbour wall won over the younger fishermen.
examples.zh: 他「强硬激进的」防波堤保卫主张赢得了年轻渔民的拥护。

words.enDefinition: specific form of evildoing

examples.en: Gambling was the vice that emptied the eldest brother's farm savings.
examples.zh: 赌博这个「恶习」掏空了大哥的农场积蓄。

examples.en: The village had few vices beyond gossip and the occasional card game.
examples.zh: 村里除了闲言碎语和偶尔打牌，几乎没有别的「恶习」。

words.enDefinition: with anxiety or apprehension

examples.en: Parents waited anxiously outside the exam hall until the last bell.
examples.zh: 家长们「焦急地」在考场外守到最后一遍铃响。

examples.en: The fisherman watched anxiously as the storm clouds gathered over the bay.
examples.zh: 乌云在港湾上空聚拢，渔民「忧心忡忡地」注视着。

words.enDefinition: to a faint degree or weakly perceived

examples.en: Music played faintly from the harbour cafe as the boats came in.
examples.zh: 渔船归港时，港口咖啡馆的音乐「隐隐约约地」传来。

examples.en: The old photograph showed the church tower only faintly through the fog.
examples.zh: 雾气里，老照片上的教堂钟楼只「隐约可辨」。

words.enDefinition: roll of photographic film holding a series of frames to be projected by a movie projector

examples.en: Grandfather threads the film reel onto the projector with steady hands.
examples.zh: 爷爷手法平稳，把电影「胶片盘」装上放映机。

examples.en: The fishing reel squeaks when the mackerel pull hard on the line.
examples.zh: 鲭鱼猛拽钓线时，渔线「卷线轮」会吱吱作响。

words.enDefinition: without justice or fairness

examples.en: The letter was wrongly delivered to the bakery instead of the school.
examples.zh: 那封信被「误投」到了面包房，而不是学校。

examples.en: He was wrongly blamed for the broken gate until the neighbours spoke up.
examples.zh: 邻居开口澄清前，损坏的大门一直被「错怪」到他头上。

words.enDefinition: in a cheerful manner

examples.en: The baker greets every customer cheerfully, even at five in the morning.
examples.zh: 哪怕清晨五点，面包师傅也「乐呵呵地」招呼每位顾客。

examples.en: She cheerfully admits that her first loaf was hard as a brick.
examples.zh: 她「爽快地」承认，自己烤的第一条面包硬得像砖头。

words.enDefinition: in a cold unemotional manner

examples.en: The clerk answered coldly, so we took our complaint to the manager.
examples.zh: 职员回话「冷冰冰的」，我们便向经理投诉。

examples.en: The wind blew coldly across the pier all through the fishing season.
examples.zh: 整个捕鱼季，海风都在码头上「冷冷地」吹着。

words.enDefinition: the official currency of the euro area, used by eurozone members of the European Union

examples.en: The ferry tickets cost forty euro for two bicycles included.
examples.zh: 连两辆自行车在内，轮渡票一共四十「欧元」。

examples.en: The stall accepts euro cash but prefers the local card payment.
examples.zh: 摊位收「欧元」现金，但更希望刷本地银行卡。

words.enDefinition: with impatience; in an impatient manner

examples.en: The children waited impatiently for the ice-cream van to turn the corner.
examples.zh: 孩子们「不耐烦地」等着冰淇淋车拐过街角。

examples.en: He tapped his fingers impatiently while the printer slowly warmed up.
examples.zh: 打印机慢慢预热时，他不「耐烦地」敲着手指。

words.enDefinition: with confidence; in a confident manner

examples.en: She confidently ordered dinner in Portuguese on the first evening abroad.
examples.zh: 出国头一晚，她就「自信地」用葡萄牙语点了菜。

examples.en: The young skipper confidently steered the ferry into the narrow harbour mouth.
examples.zh: 年轻的船长「沉着地」把轮渡驶进狭窄的港口入口。

words.enDefinition: in a generous manner

examples.en: The farmer generously gave the choir a crate of apples for the concert.
examples.zh: 农场主「慷慨地」送给合唱团一箱苹果，供音乐会用。

examples.en: They generously opened their garden to the neighbours every spring.
examples.zh: 每年春天他们都「大方地」向邻居们开放自家花园。

words.enDefinition: in a cheap manner

examples.en: You can eat cheaply at the workers' canteen near the station.
examples.zh: 在车站附近的工人食堂吃饭很「便宜」。

examples.en: The shed was built cheaply from leftover pallets and old corrugated iron.
examples.zh: 这个棚子用剩余托盘和旧瓦楞铁皮「低成本地」搭了起来。

words.enDefinition: in a cheerful manner

examples.en: The guests chatted pleasantly on the terrace until the candles burned low.
examples.zh: 客人们在露台上「愉快地」闲谈，直到蜡烛烧短。

examples.en: The innkeeper pleasantly waived the extra charge for the late arrival.
examples.zh: 客栈老板「和气地」免掉了晚到的加收费用。

words.enDefinition: in a stiff manner

examples.en: The new boots made him walk stiffly for the first week.
examples.zh: 新靴子让他头一周走路都「僵硬」。

examples.en: The old major bowed stiffly to the memorial and laid his wreath.
examples.zh: 年迈的少校「僵硬地」向纪念碑鞠躬，献上了花圈。

words.enDefinition: in an unfair manner

examples.en: The referee unfairly booked our keeper for something he never did.
examples.zh: 裁判「不公平地」给我们门将出牌，他根本没做那事。

examples.en: Rents rise unfairly fast in villages near the new ferry terminal.
examples.zh: 轮渡码头附近的村庄，房租涨得「不合理地」快。

words.enDefinition: spoken with poor articulation as if with a thick tongue

examples.en: Grandmother spread the butter thickly on the warm crusty loaf.
examples.zh: 奶奶在温热的脆皮面包上「厚厚地」抹了一层黄油。

examples.en: The fog lay thickly over the harbour until nearly noon.
examples.zh: 浓雾「厚厚地」笼罩港口，快到中午才散。
